:JUDGMENT:
This is a Petition filed under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act seeking Compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- for the death of Divakar S/o A Ramakrishna Reddy in the Road Traffic Accident.
The wife, Minor son and parents of deceased Divakar have filed this petition.

2. The brief averments made in the Petition are as under:
That on 01.01.2021 at about 4.00 p.m., on Bangalore- Mulbagal Road - NH-75 near Shankara Reddy Farm, Mulbagal Taluk, Kolar District,
Divakar (deceased) was driving his Car bearing no.KA-01-P-1500 from Bangalore to Gummalapura village.
Due to mechanical defect, the car dashed against the Road Divider.
As a result, all the occupants of the car sustained injuries.
Divakar also sustained grievous-injuries and he was shifted to R.L.Jalappa Hospital, Kolar, and then to Vikram Hospital where he succumbed to the injuries.
3. That prior to accident, Divakar was hale and healthy and was earning Rs.25,000/- per month from his vegetable business.
4. That during his life-time, Divakar had purchased the car from respondent no.1 and since then was using it as the Owner.
That Respondent no.1 has insured the Car with Respondent no.2 under Compulsory Personal Accident Cover of Rs.15,00,000/-
Thus the petitioners are entitled for the same from respondent no.2.
Hence this petition.

5. In pursuance of service of notice to the respondents, they appeared before the court.

However,
respondent no.2 alone filed objections to the main petition.
6. In the Objection Statement of Respondent no.2- Insurance Company, the petition-averments are denied.
It is contended that the person driving the vehicle has "No relation in force" to drive the vehicle as on the date of accident.

7. It is specifically contended that the petition is liable to be dismissed since the accident is due to the negligence of the deceased himself and the Police have filed the "abated charge sheet' against him.
Further, that the driver of the car was not holding a valid and effective driving license at the time of accident.
8. Further, the owner of the insured car has not intimated the alleged accident to respondent no.2 and has violated Section 134(c) and 158(6) of Motor Vehicles Act.
On these grounds, Respondent no.2 has prayed to dismiss the petition against it.

9. On the rival pleadings, the following Issues have been framed:
ISSUES 1. Whether the Petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles act is maintainable?
2. What Order?

ADDL. ISSUES 1. Whether the petitioner proves that late Divakar met with self-accident on 01.01.2021 at about 4.00 p.m. near Shankar Reddy farm, Mulbagal Taluk, Kolar district, while he was driving a car bearing registration No.KA-01-P-1500 and died?
2.
Whether the petitioners proves that they are entitled for personal accident coverage amount of Rs.15,00,000/- from the Respondent No.2?
10. On behalf of petitioners, Petitioner no.1 has got herself examined as P.W.1 and has got marked Exs.P.1 to 16.
On the other hand, the Respondents have neither cross-examined PW.1 nor have adduced any evidence.
11. Perused the pleadings and evidence on record.
Heard both-sides.

12. My answer to the Issues are as under :
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative  Addl. Issue No.1 & 2 : In the Affirmative G.A. Pushpa vs Harisha.

 for the following :

13. Issue No.1 & Addl. Issue No.1, 2: These issues warrant common discussion and hence are taken-up together to avoid repetition of facts.
It is the case of Petitioners that one Divakar who is the husband of petitioner no.1, father of petitioner no.2 and son of petitioner no.3 & 4 has died in the Road Traffic Accident.
14. On behalf of petitioners, Petitioner no.1 has got herself examined as P.W.1 and has got marked Exs.P.1 to 16.

Exs. P.1 to 11 are the true copy of FIR, Complaint, Police Intimation, Spot Mahazar,
Sketch, IMV report, Inquest, PM report, Charge sheet, Aadhar Cards.

15. On going through the FIR & Complaint at Ex.P.1 and the Spot Mahazar at Ex.P.2, it is clear that except the Car bearing no.KA-01-P-1500 which was driven by Divakar (deceased), no other vehicle is involved in the alleged accident.

When the accident is not due to any mechanical defect of the said Car as per the IMV Report at Ex.P.3, the fact that Divakar - the driver of the said Car himself has hit the Road Divider, proves his 'negligence'.
Ex.P.4 is the Inquest.
Ex.P.5 is the Post Mortem Report, which shows that death is due to shock as a result of injury to Brain.
Ex.P.6 is the Charge-sheet filed against deceased Divakar for the offences punishable under Sections 279, 338 & 304A of IPC.
Ex.P.7 is the notarized copy of Aadhar card of deceased Divakar; Exs.P.8 to 11 are the notarized copy of Aadhar cards of petitioners.
Exs.P.12 & 13 are the Medical Bills and Prescriptions.

16. In support of their contention that they are the legal- representatives of deceased Divakar, the Aadhar Cards of deceased Divakar and petitioner no.1 to 4 have been produced as per Exs.P.7 to 11,
the contents of which prove their relationship with deceased Divakar.
Moreover there is no dispute with regard to the relationship.
As per the FIR & Complaint at Ex.P.1, Divakar was stated to have been driving his Car.
Ex.P.15 is the Driving Licence of deceased Divakar which is valid as on the date of accident.
But as already discussed above, in view of RC & Insurance at Exs.P.14 & 16, deceased Divakar cannot be held to be the Owner of the said Car.
If not the Owner of the said Car, then who was Divakar who was the driving the Car at the time of accident ??
He should be the 'Borrower' of the said Car.
18. In the background of these facts, the question is, whether the present petition filed under Section 166 of M.V.Act by the legal-representatives of deceased Divakar, is maintainable??

In this regard,
the learned counsel for petitioners has relied-on the decision reported in: 2014 ACJ 721 - High Court of Madras - Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Co. Ltd., Vs. C Ramesh: The Hon'ble Madras High Court based on the decisions of the Hon'ble Apex Court, has held as under:
1. Motor Insurance - Personal Accident Cover - Negligence of owner cum driver - Vehicle was insured and on payment of additional premium, personal accident cover to owner cum driver was provided -

entities.text: 2014 ACJ 721 - High Court of Madras - Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Co. Ltd., Vs. C Ramesh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Whether injured or legal-representatives of the deceased owner cum driver have to prove that there was no negligence or neglect or fault on the part of owner cum driver for claiming compensation - Held: No; Policy is personal to the holder and it is not indemnify the loss suffered by others.

2. Claims Tribunal - Consumer Forum - Jurisdiction - Motor Insurance - Personal Accident Cover - Liability of Insurance Company - Personal Accident Policy is taken to cover the risks of personal injury or death of insured in accident caused due to use of vehicle in a public place -

entities.text: Claims Tribunal - Consumer Forum - Jurisdiction - Motor Insurance - Personal Accident Cover - Liability of Insurance Company - Personal Accident Policy
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Whether jurisdiction to claim compensation for injury or death of insured covered under personal insurance policy would lie before the Claims Tribunal under Motor Vehicles Act - Held: Yes; there is no need for the injured/legal- representative of the deceased to approach the Consumer Forum.

Thus from the above it is clear that, the present claim petition based on the Personal Accident Cover is maintainable before this Tribunal, and there is no necessity for the Claimants to prove the aspect of negligence also.

But admittedly, in view of 'Abated Charge sheet' at Ex.P.6 being filed against Deceased Diwakar, his legal-representatives could not have filed the petition under Section 163-A of M.V.Act; and hence they have chosen to file this petition under Section 166 of M.V.Act, merely on G.A. 5 the basis of Personal Accident Cover of Rs.15,00,000/- provided under the Policy at Ex.P.16 to the 'Owner Driver'.
However as already discussed above, deceased Divakar cannot be held to be the Owner of the said Car, and at the most he is the 'borrower' of the same.

19. Then the next question would be, whether the legal- representatives of the 'borrower' of said car can maintain this claim petition on the basis of the Personal Accident Cover provided to the 'Owner Driver' under the Policy at Ex.P.16??

The answer is 'Yes' in view of the dictum laid-down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Ramkhiladi's Case reported in 2020 ACJ 627 (Ramkhiladi & Another Vs.
United India Insurance Co. Ltd., & Another): Wherein the Hon'ble Apex Court has observed that 'the borrower of the vehicle steps into the shoes of the owner'.

sentences.text: Thus from the discussion made supra, in view of the Insurance Policy at Ex.P.16, the Petitioners are entitled to fixed compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- with costs and interest at 6% p.a. from the date of the Petition till realization.
Accordingly, Respondents no.2 - Insurance Company is liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.

Accordingly, I answer Issue No.1 in the "Affirmative" and Addl.
Issue No.1, 2 also in the "Affirmative".

20. Issue No.2 : In the result, I proceed to pass the following :
ORDER
The Petition under Section 166 of M.V. Act is allowed with costs.
A sum of Rs.15,00,000/- (Rupees Fifteen Lakhs only) is awarded as total compensation to the petitioners with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its payment.
Respondent no.2 shall deposit the compensation amount to the court within 60 days from the date of this judgment.
Petitioner no.1 is entitled to 40% of the total compensation amount awarded.

Out of which 50% of the award amount is ordered to be released to Petitioner no.1 by way of E-Payment after proper identification, and the remaining 50% shall be kept in Fixed deposit in the name of Petitioner no.1 in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank of her choice for a period of 3 years.
Petitioner no.2 is entitled to 30% out of the total compensation amount awarded.
The entire amount awarded to Petitioner no.2 is ordered to be kept as F.D. in his name in any Nationalised bank till he attains the age of majority.
Petitioner no.3 is entitled to 10% & Petitioner no.4 is entitled to 20% out of the total compensation amount awarded.
The entire amount awarded to Petitioner no.3 & 4 is ordered to be released in their favour.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs. 1,000/-.
